deck_context.source_summary: Class 16 begins Week 4 of a traditional AEM Sites course for frontend-oriented developers. It builds the minimum Java runtime vocabulary needed before Sling Models: core module, OSGi bundle, Declarative Services component, service contract, runtime states and Sling Resource API.
deck_context.core_claim: Compiled Java becomes an AEM capability only after bundle packaging and resolution, Declarative Services lifecycle requirements and a correct content boundary; diagnose each handoff with observable runtime evidence.
canonical_facts: The Maven core module produces the project's OSGi bundle JAR.
A bundle manifest declares symbolic identity, version, imported packages and exported packages.
Successful Java compilation does not prove that Apache Felix can resolve runtime package imports.
A bundle, a Declarative Services component and a registered service are different runtime objects.
A plain Java class inside a bundle is not automatically an OSGi component or service.
@Component declares a Declarative Services component and @Reference expresses a service dependency.
Required references and required configuration must be satisfied before a component can activate.
A bundle can be Active while a contained component remains unsatisfied.
The local AEM SDK exposes the Web Console; cloud environments expose read-only runtime evidence through Developer Console.
A Resource exposes a path, name, resource type, properties and children without requiring direct JCR Node use.
ValueMap supports typed property access and adaptTo bridges a Resource to supported higher-level abstractions.
Prefer AEM product APIs, then Sling abstractions; use JCR only for JCR-specific needs and OSGi for container concerns.
Administrative repository access is not allowed; background access uses a scoped service user and a correctly closed ResourceResolver.
AEM as a Cloud Service treats deployed code and configuration as immutable at runtime.

slides.title: Java crosses several boundaries before AEM can use it.
slides.intent: Prevent successful compilation from being treated as proof that AEM can execute the class.
key_points: Java source lives in the Maven core module.
Compilation produces bytecode; bundle packaging adds OSGi metadata.
Apache Felix resolves runtime package dependencies.
Declarative Services creates eligible components and binds references.
Application code then consumes AEM or Sling objects such as Resource.

local_context.required_background: Show exactly six stages: SOURCE, COMPILE, BUNDLE JAR, FELIX RESOLUTION, DS COMPONENT, RESOURCE-BACKED BEHAVIOR. Under them show evidence: .java, .class, MANIFEST.MF, package wiring, component state, Resource path/properties. Conclude BUILD SUCCESS IS ONLY ONE CHECKPOINT.

layout.composition: One horizontal six-stage pipeline with an evidence rail below and one strong conclusion banner.
layout.intent: Make the runtime handoffs visible as a sequence.

constraints: Use the exact six stage names from local_context.
Keep each stage to one concise evidence label.
Do not introduce Sling Model injection.

slides.title: An OSGi bundle is a managed JAR.
slides.intent: Distinguish a normal JAR from an OSGi module whose runtime contracts are enforced.
key_points: Bundle-SymbolicName and Bundle-Version create runtime identity.
Import-Package declares packages required at runtime.
Export-Package publishes intended cross-bundle contracts.
Compilation may succeed while Felix cannot resolve an import.
Keep implementation packages private.

local_context.required_background: Use a fictional wknd.core bundle. Show exact manifest labels Bundle-SymbolicName: com.adobe.aem.guides.wknd.core, Bundle-Version, Import-Package, Export-Package. Contrast COMPILE PASS with RUNTIME UNRESOLVED when one required package provider is missing or incompatible.

layout.composition: Large bundle cutaway on the left, manifest contract in the center and compile-versus-runtime comparison on the right.
layout.intent: Connect bundle contents and manifest wiring to a concrete failure.

visual_elements.main_visual: Managed JAR cutaway plus package-wiring sockets.

constraints: Spell all manifest headers exactly.
Do not imply every package should be exported.
Use only one concise fictional package mismatch.

slides.title: Bundle, component and service are different runtime objects.
slides.intent: Establish the three runtime concepts developers must keep separate.
key_points: A bundle is a managed JAR and class-loading boundary.
A component is an object managed by Declarative Services.
A service is a capability published by contract.
One bundle can contain many components.
One component may publish zero, one or many services.

slides.title: Declarative Services activates only satisfied components.
slides.intent: Explain why runtime collaboration is declared instead of manually constructed.
key_points: @Component declares a class for Declarative Services.
@Reference expresses a dependency on a service contract.
Required references and configuration must be satisfied before activation.
Activation and deactivation belong to the container lifecycle.
Do not keep durable business state in the component instance.

layout.intent: Make dependency satisfaction the cause of activation.

visual_elements.main_visual: UNSATISFIED → reference bound → ACTIVE → deactivate lifecycle.

constraints: Render @Component and @Reference exactly.

slides.title: Runtime state tells you which boundary failed.
slides.intent: Turn bundle and component states into evidence-driven troubleshooting.
key_points: Installed commonly points to unresolved package requirements.
Resolved means wiring exists but the bundle is not active.
Active bundle does not prove every component is satisfied.
Unsatisfied component points to a missing reference or required configuration.
Use Web Console locally and Developer Console in cloud environments.

local_context.required_background: Create two separate diagnostic rails. Bundle rail: INSTALLED → inspect missing imports; RESOLVED → inspect start state; ACTIVE → bundle lifecycle is available. Component rail: UNSATISFIED → inspect missing references or required configuration; ACTIVE → component is available. Bottom environment split: LOCAL SDK /system/console is interactive; CLOUD Developer Console is read-only evidence.

layout.composition: Two state rails with symptom/evidence/action rows, then a local-versus-cloud inspection footer.
layout.intent: Prevent bundle state and component state from being conflated.

visual_elements.main_visual: Runtime diagnostic matrix with state lights and console inspectors.

constraints: Keep bundle and component states in separate labeled sections.
Do not claim Developer Console can mutate production runtime state.
Do not recommend reinstalling before inspecting evidence.

slides.title: The Resource API is the default content boundary.
slides.intent: Connect Java runtime foundations to the primary content object used next.
key_points: Resource represents an addressable item in Sling's resource tree.
It exposes path, name, resource type, properties and children.
ValueMap provides typed property access with explicit defaults.
Child navigation follows known content structure.
adaptTo bridges to supported higher-level abstractions.

slides.title: Choose the highest useful API.
slides.intent: Avoid coupling ordinary component code to lower-level repository or container APIs.
key_points: Prefer an AEM product abstraction when it directly models the requirement.
Otherwise prefer Sling resources and requests.
Use JCR only for JCR-specific capabilities.
Use OSGi for container concerns.
Background access uses a scoped service user and a correctly closed ResourceResolver.

slides.title: Key takeaways
slides.intent: Consolidate the minimum backend vocabulary and diagnostic habits needed next.
key_points: core source becomes usable only after compilation, bundle resolution and component activation.

Prefer AEM and Sling abstractions; use Resource API for ordinary content access.
